summary:
**SPACE RELICS — Not Everything We Sent Came Back**

SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital museum that explores humanity's robotic and scientific missions to the Moon and Mars. The project focuses on spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments that have been left behind on these celestial bodies, preserving the stories of space exploration beyond the end of a mission.

The platform features five modules: Mission Chronicles, an interactive mission timeline; Learning Zone, with educational quizzes; Science Lab, for comparing gravity on Earth, the Moon and Mars; Observatory, showcasing planetary missions and imagery; and Research Archive, providing access to space research resources.

Developed using React, Vite, JavaScript, CSS and NASA's Image and Video Library API, SPACE RELICS combines technology, science and interactive learning to make planetary exploration accessible and engaging for students and space enthusiasts.

SPACE RELICS — Project Details

Project Title: SPACE RELICS
Tagline: Not everything we sent came back.
Domain: Space Exploration, Astronomy and Education
Platform: Interactive Web Application
Target Users: Students, educators, researchers and space enthusiasts.

1. Project Overview

SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital museum that documents the history of human and robotic exploration of the Moon and Mars. It focuses on the spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific equipment sent on planetary missions, including the objects that remain on these celestial bodies after their missions end.

The platform presents space exploration information through interactive timelines, educational activities, scientific experiments, mission imagery and research resources.

2. Problem Statement

Information about space missions, their achievements, landing locations and the equipment left behind is distributed across different sources. There is no single engaging platform within this project that brings these elements together for easy exploration and learning.

SPACE RELICS addresses this by organising mission-related information into an accessible and interactive digital experience.

3. Project Objectives

  • Document important Moon and Mars exploration missions.
  • Highlight spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments left behind.
  • Make space science more accessible through interactive learning.
  • Present mission histories in a structured visual format.
  • Provide access to trusted space research resources.
  • Encourage curiosity about planetary science and space engineering.

4. Core Modules and Features

Module

Description

Mission Chronicles

Interactive timeline of lunar and Martian missions, including mission details and achievements.

Learning Zone

Educational quizzes and activities about space exploration.

Science Lab

Interactive gravity comparison between Earth, Moon and Mars.

Observatory

Visual exploration of spacecraft, rovers, landers and mission imagery.

Research Archive

Research resources and official links from NASA, ISRO and JAXA.

5. Technology Stack

  • Frontend: React.js
  • Build Tool: Vite
  • Programming Language: JavaScript
  • Styling: CSS
  • Animations: Motion
  • Icons: Lucide React
  • 3D and Visualisation: Three.js and React Three Fiber
  • Mapping: Leaflet and React Leaflet
  • Space Imagery: NASA Image and Video Library API
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub
  • Deployment: Vercel

6. Expected Outcome

The expected outcome is a responsive, interactive web platform that allows users to explore planetary missions, understand the technologies involved, learn scientific concepts and discover the physical traces of space exploration.

7. Future Scope

  • Add more lunar and Martian missions.
  • Introduce detailed 3D models of spacecraft and rovers.
  • Develop interactive maps showing mission landing locations.
  • Integrate additional scientific datasets.
  • Expand the archive to include other planetary exploration missions.
  • Introduce more interactive simulations and educational activities.

8. Project Vision

SPACE RELICS aims to preserve and present the stories of humanity's exploration beyond Earth. It highlights an important idea: a space mission does not disappear from history when communication stops or its operational life ends. The machines and instruments left behind become part of the story of human exploration.

SPACE RELICS — Exploring the missions, discovering the machines, preserving what remains. 🌕
